**Invented for development and tests. Not BMW data, not real customer quotes.** Real BMW files go in
`data/raw/`, which is gitignored.

Regenerate them with `node data/samples/generate.ts` (Node ≥ 23.6). They imitate what BMW exports
might look like, including the awkward parts the Raw block has to handle:

| File                       | Raw block "Dataset" | Format                                                                                                  | What the Raw block makes of it                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `customer_feedback.csv`    | Customer feedback   | UTF-8 with BOM, `,`, quoted comments with commas, quotes and a line break; de/en/fr/it/es               | 35 records (one per comment, language and market per row); the row without a comment is skipped and reported                   |
| `equipment_take_rates.csv` | Equipment data      | German Excel export: `;`, decimal commas, Windows-1252, German headers (`Ausstattung`, `Einbaurate %`) | 17 records; 8 usage findings (take rate ≥ 70 % → expected as standard, ≤ 15 % → rarely chosen); the row without a rate is reported |
| `sales_volumes.csv`        | Sales volumes       | `,`, one row per derivative and year                                                                    | 12 records; 2 findings (volume change ≥ 10 % between first and last year); the i5 Touring launch (0 units in 2023) is noted        |
| `customer_study.xlsx`      | Customer study      | Excel workbook with two sheets: `Results` (scores) and `Verbatims` (free text)                          | Sheet empty → first sheet (7 records); sheet `Verbatims` → 6 records with languages                                             |

How columns are recognised (English and German names): `packages/blocks/src/raw/columns.ts`.

BMW's real files stay in `data/raw/` (gitignored). When they're there, `npm test` also runs the
"BMW …" suites in `packages/blocks/src/raw/raw.test.ts` (structure checks only) and `npm run smoke`
previews them in the app. To try them by hand: `npm run dev`, add a Raw block, choose the file.

+- **Request:** Highlight a clicked car part with a subtle blue shade; commit and push when finished.
+Selected parts use the app's `--color-brand-soft` token instead of an almost invisible blend.
+Sketch lines stay visible, deselection restores normal colours, and interior ghosting and glass
+masks are preserved. Added 18 synthetic regressions covering light/dark themes and selection states.
+Verified an isolated snapshot containing only this change:
+- `npm run typecheck && npm test`: passed; 265 tests passed, 25 skipped.
+- `npm run smoke`: passed; 29 screenshots, selected door visually checked.
+The shared checkout had a concurrent geometry-test failure. That unrelated work was not modified
+or included in the code commit. The code commit was pushed to `codex/car-model-refinements`.
+OpenCode session export produced with `session export --sanitize` after the code was pushed.
+It is not a reconstructed conversation. Sensitive transcript/file payloads are removed by the
+exporter. No BMW dataset contents or API keys are included.
+Entire reported no tracked session and the code commit has no checkpoint trailer. This explicit
+sanitized export is provided under `.entire/` as requested; it is not presented as a native Entire
+checkpoint. Existing hooks and tracking configuration are unchanged.
+# Car menu and marker work log
+- Scope: Car-tab navigation and menu-driven markers (WS3).
+- Record type: manually reconstructed work log, not an Entire checkpoint or full transcript.
+1. Make Exterior and Interior expandable and add general subclasses with detailed parts,
+   including Doors. Commit and push to the current branch.
+   - Added expandable Exterior, Interior and Technology sections and subclasses such as
+     Doors, Body & design, Lighting, Windows & mirrors, Seats and Cockpit & controls.
+   - Kept existing detailed part IDs, requirement classification and part selection.
+   - Added rolled-up requirement counts and navigation coverage tests.
+   - Commit: `05cc7b8` — `ws3: add expandable car parts submenus`.
+2. Start with every menu closed; opening a class activates its markings. Above eight
+   markings, use small blue points; otherwise retain normal text and counts.
+   - Menus now load collapsed and no markers are shown initially.
+   - Opening a class shows its descendant parts, including parts without requirements.
+   - Opening a subclass narrows marker focus. Closing it restores its parent; closing
+     the active top-level class clears its markers and closes its child menus.

content.content:
## The building blocks

Each block is specified as **Block (params / inner workplace / inputs / outputs)**, e.g. HIL (t/f/1/1)
= has parameters, no inner workplace, 1 input, 1 output. "n" = one port per entry of a list parameter.
Blocks are finalized one at a time; **State** says how far each one is.

| Block           | Spec         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | State                                                                                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Custom**      | (f/t/1/1)    | An empty block. Build any sub-flow inside it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  | placeholder                                                                                                                  |
| **Raw**         | (t/f/0/1)    | Brings in Excel (.xlsx), CSV, Research JSON or a SQLite query as one unified data stream: one record per row (repeated feedback rows merged), report-style sheets read by section, plus usage findings from take rates and sales volumes. "Preview data" shows the parsed result right away.                                                                                                                                                                                   | **built**: .xlsx, CSV, JSON, SQLite; reads BMW's exports; runs in a flow once the executor exists (WS1)                      |
| **Research**    | (t/t/0/1)    | Searches the web; emits a data stream in the same format as Raw.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | placeholder params                                                                                                           |
| **AI Filter**   | (t/t/1/1)    | Keeps the items that match a criterion written in plain language.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | placeholder params                                                                                                           |
| **AI Splitter** | (t/t/1/2–10) | Routes each primary item while retaining linked evidence. Raw-data modes analyze customer demand into 2–10 bands, fixed car-part groups or custom global groups; legacy priority, category, sentiment and custom-instruction routing remain supported. An untouched inner workplace uses built-in routing; adding blocks or connections overrides it with a sub-flow.                                                                                                          | **built**: standalone Mastra Agent through the injected `LlmClient`, plus offline mock; report and paused-HIL routing review |
| **HIL**         | (t/f/1/1)    | Human in the loop (capacitor icon). The flow waits here until a person has reviewed what arrived, then passes it on. **Double-click opens the review report:** a flow chart of how the data was collected (every step it passed through, across inner workplaces) and a table icon on every step to see the data at that point.                                                                                                                                                | **finalized** — report and pause/continue logic built; runs once the executor exists (WS1)                                   |
| **Add to Car**  | (t/f/n/0)    | AI agents turn what arrives into requirements for the successor. Inputs **1. Priority … n. Priority** (the input an item arrives on sets its ranking) and **context inputs** (Auto, or Sales volumes) that are background only. Analysts, a synthesizer, an architect and a critic write and review each requirement; a judge rates it, and every requirement gets a **confidence score**. The block's **thought process** view shows, step by step, how the agents got there. | **built**: agents on any API setup from Settings, offline mock without a key; `npm run eval:f70`                             |

Spec and ports: `packages/core/src/blocks.ts`. Implementations: `packages/blocks/src/<block>/`.

Legacy splitter routing uses the most advanced populated layer (requirements, then themes, findings or
records) exactly once. Supporting evidence can appear on multiple branches. Unlinked upstream

## The building blocks (`packages/core/src/blocks.ts`)

A workflow is a tree of **workplaces**. Each workplace holds blocks and edges. Seven kinds of block
are in the palette, defined once in `BLOCK_SPECS` (label, description, group, params, ports, whether
it has an inner workplace):

| Block       | Ports                                 | Inner workplace | Params (placeholders for now)                                                   |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Custom      | 1 in · 1 out                          | yes             | none                                                                            |
| Raw         | no input · 1 out (data stream)        | no              | Excel/CSV/SQLite or Research JSON import, dataset, file/query                   |
| Research    | no input · 1 out (same format as Raw) | yes             | question, source types, market, age, results                                    |
| AI Filter   | 1 in · 1 out (kept)                   | yes             | criterion, model, min. confidence                                               |
| AI Splitter | 1 in · 2–10 outputs                   | yes             | customer priority, car parts, custom or legacy routing, branches, model         |
| HIL         | 1 in · 1 out                          | no              | reviewer, instructions, approvals, edits                                        |
| Add to Car  | one in **per priority** + context ins | no              | priorities, contexts (Auto / Sales volumes), max. requirements, vehicle, market |

## WS8 — Prioritization

**Status:** open · **Owner:** — · **Branch:** —
**Depends on:** nothing; agree the function signature with WS7 in your log.

**Tasks**

- [ ] Deterministic factors in `packages/blocks/src/prioritization/`: customer impact, evidence
      strength, competitive gap, trend momentum, each with a one-line note.
- [ ] LLM-judged factors (brand fit, ease) behind `LlmClient`, one-line note each; mock in tests.
- [ ] `priorityRationale` naming the top drivers; flag "high score, weak evidence".
- [ ] Tests: reproducible scores on the fixtures; changing Settings weights changes the ranking as expected.
- [ ] Export the function the AI Splitter's priority mode calls (`weightedTotal` + `priorityForScore`).

import re
# ARCHITECTURE
p='docs/ARCHITECTURE.md'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("A workflow is a tree of **workplaces**. Each workplace holds blocks and edges. Seven kinds of block","A workflow is a tree of **workplaces**. Each workplace holds blocks and edges. Eight kinds of block")
old='''| Add to Car  | one in **per priority** + context ins | no              | priorities, contexts (Auto / Sales volumes), max. requirements, vehicle, market |'''
new='''| Add to Car  | one in **per priority** + context ins | no              | priorities, contexts (Auto / Sales volumes), max. requirements, vehicle, market |
| Analytics   | one in **per named input** · 1 out    | no              | inputs (1–8, named), country/time column overrides, timeline buckets, phrases   |'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
# Add a section after "## HIL review report" block? append before "## AI Splitter: raw analysis"
anchor='## AI Splitter: raw analysis and review'
section='''## Analytics block and view

The Analytics block (`analytics`, group `insight`) counts what its inputs carry, **by rules only**:
no model call anywhere. At run time it logs what each input carried and passes all inputs on,
merged (`packages/blocks/src/analytics/`). The charts are computed in the renderer
(`components/analytics/`), so filters and comparisons answer instantly:

- **Loading** (`load.ts`): per input port, the saved `runs.blockOutput` of every block wired into it
  when a run contains the block; before a run, a direct source (Raw, Research without a sub-flow)
  is read with `blocks.preview`, and an input behind a transforming block says it needs a run.
- **Dataset** (`engine/dataset.ts`): column roles are detected **per source file** from header
  names and values (country, time, person ID, sentiment/feedback type, classifications, year
  columns such as `volume_2030` as a series with plan years) or taken from the block's params, and
  every detection is written to `notes`. Countries normalise to ISO codes (`countries.ts`), times
  parse to UTC buckets (`time.ts`), topics come from an English/German keyword lexicon
  (`topics.ts`), sentiment from the data's own classification column or a word list with negation
  (`sentiment.ts`), phrase queries match whole words with `*` and `|` (`text.ts`).
- **Counting** (`engine/aggregate.ts`): records and distinct people per key, time series, cross
  tabs, phrase stats, two-proportion z-tests for comparisons (marked only when p < 0.05 with
  enough records), and Sankey flow data.
- **View** (`AnalyticsView.tsx`): opens full screen from the block's chart button or a
  double-click; tabs Overview, Countries, Timeline, What people say, Topics & sentiment, Compare
  sources, Flow and Data quality, one filter bar for all of them. Charts are hand-written SVG in
  the BMW M colorway (`--color-viz-*` tokens, CVD-checked in light and dark), each with a table view.

'''
assert anchor in s
s=s.replace(anchor, section+anchor,1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

# PRODUCT
p='PRODUCT.md'
s=open(p).read()
lines=s.split('\n')
idx=[i for i,l in enumerate(lines) if l.startswith('| **Add to Car**  |')][0]
row='| **Analytics**   | (t/f/n/1)    | Counts what its inputs carry, **by rules only (no AI)**: by country, over time, by topic and sentiment, how many people say a phrase (with their own words), and how data sources differ (significance-tested). One input per named entry (default one; "Add input" on the block); opens **full screen** with flow charts, pie charts, heatmaps and timelines in the BMW M colours. Time is used as soon as a dataset has a date/month/year column. | **built**: 8 tabs, per-source column detection, template "Compare feedback sources", native smoke |'
lines.insert(idx+1,row)
open(p,'w').write('\n'.join(lines))

s=open(p).read()
